_provenance.label: synthetic: built to OpenRouter's documented type; NOT a recording
_provenance.why: The recorded live response (openrouter_chat_completion.json, 2026-09-26) reports cache_write_tokens: 0, so it cannot show that cache writes are priced at their own rate. This fixture keeps that mapping covered without editing the recording.

sources.what: documented_usage_example below, copied verbatim (also preserved in the recorded fixture's documented_usage_example): prompt_tokens 194 with cache_write_tokens 100, i.e. cache writes reported as a part of prompt_tokens. 'cache_write_tokens is the number of tokens that were written to the cache (only returned for models with explicit caching and cache write pricing)'
the non-streaming Response / ResponseUsage type the response below is built to
qwen/qwen3.8-flash prices: prompt 0.15, completion 0.47, input_cache_read 0.016, input_cache_write 0.2 (USD per million tokens)

_provenance.how_response_was_built: The counts were chosen by the drafter so that cached_tokens and cache_write_tokens are both non-zero, and both are treated as parts of prompt_tokens (the documented example's reading; the recorded response has 1408 cached out of 1920 prompt). cost is these counts at the listed qwen/qwen3.8-flash rates: 2000 uncached x 0.15 + 9000 read x 0.016 + 1000 written x 0.2 + 800 output x 0.47, per million = 0.00102.
